{{Quote|Something has happened in Tetsubal. Something bad.|A Lost Tribe sentry|<ref name="paragon" />}}
'''Tetsubal''' was a [[City/Legends|city]] located in the area of the [[Ragnos Lakes]], on the continent [[Keshtah Minor]] of the remote [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]]. Located to the south of the planet's [[Capital/Legends|capital]], [[Tahv]], by [[4985 BBY]] Tetsubal had a population of 18,000 [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] natives. Tetsubal was one of eight villages around the Ragnos Lakes, and in 4,985 BBY the inhabitants of the region began to harvest a type of [[fluorescent algae]] from those [[Water/Legends|waters]]. Hoping to find a use for the algae, [[Yaru Korsin]], leader of the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]]&mdash;comprising several hundred [[Human/Legends|Humans]] and [[Sith (species)/Legends|Pureblood Sith]]&mdash;that had taken power in Kesh [[5000 BBY/Legends|fifteen years earlier]], ordered an expedition to Tetsubal and the surrounding areas to investigate. The mission was headed by [[Ravilan Wroth]], who had his own agenda&mdash;hoping to get [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] leadership to focus on finding a way off Kesh, Wroth had devised a plan to [[Poison/Legends|poison]] local water supplies with the chemical [[cyanogen silicate]], creating a fake plague that would frighten the Lost Tribe into withdrawing from Keshiri affairs. He contaminated the aqueduct that provided Tetsubal with its water, [[Death/Legends|killing]] all 18,000 of Tetsubal's residents, leaving Wroth as the only survivor. In order to contain the "infection," the remains of Tetsubal were burned to the ground. However, Wroth's treachery was discovered by Yaru Korsin's wife, [[Seelah Korsin|Seelah]], who went on to cause the deaths of the populations of the other towns in the Ragnos Lakes area and frame Wroth. As a result, Wroth and the rest of the members of the Sith [[Species/Legends|species]] among the Lost Tribe were quickly [[Red Sith Purge|executed]]. Over the ensuing centuries, Tetsubal and the rest of the towns of the Ragnos Lakes were abandoned and eventually gained a reputation as being haunted.

==Description==
{{Quote|I start in Tetsubal, farthest away.|Ravilan Wroth|<ref name="paragon" />}}
The [[City/Legends|city]] of Tetsubal was located in the [[Ragnos Lakes]] region of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh's]]<ref name="paragon" /> continent [[Keshtah Minor]].<ref name="secrets" /> Tetsubal, along with seven other villages in the area, was located to the south of the planet's [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Tahv]], and was the farthest away out of the eight towns in the area. Tetsubal was surrounded by walls, and a system of dirt roads crossed throughout the town. Tetsubal received its [[Water/Legends|water]] from a nearby aqueduct, which fed into a network of troughs that ran through the streets. Many of the village's residents lived in [[hejarbo]]-shoot huts. By [[4985 BBY]], approximately 18,000 members of Kesh's native [[Species/Legends|species]], the [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]], called Tetsubal home.<ref name="paragon" />

==History==
{{Quote|People started collapsing in restaurants, in the markets. Then the panic began.|Ravilan Wroth, describing the calamity that befell Tetsubal|<ref name="paragon" />}}
In [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], the planet Kesh was visited by a group of crash-landed [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] that claimed to be the [[Skyborn|gods]] of the indigenous Keshiri. This group of [[Human/Legends|Humans]] and [[Sith (species)/Legends|Pureblood Sith]], who came to be known as the [[Lost Tribe of Sith|Lost Tribe]], took their place as rulers of Kesh and commanded the devotion of the highly religious natives. After taking power, the Lost Tribe began a census of the planet to get an estimate of exactly how many Keshiri there were. Far to the south of the Sith crash site in the [[Takara Mountains]], Tetsubal was among the last settlements to be counted before the Sith gave up. [[4985 BBY|Fifteen years later]], a group of Keshiri from the Ragnos Lakes area began harvesting a type of [[fluorescent algae]]&mdash;believing that the specimens could perhaps be used to light Sith structures, Lost Tribe leader [[Yaru Korsin]] sent a team of subordinates, led by prominent Pureblood Sith [[Ravilan Wroth]], to investigate. Tetsubal, farthest away from the center of Sith power in Tahv, was to be visited first. However, Wroth saw that as an opportunity to put a secret plan of his into action. Using the deadly chemical [[cyanogen silicate]], Wroth [[Poison/Legends|poisoned]] Tetsubal's water supply in order to create the appearance of a plague that he could use to pressure Sith leadership to withdraw from Keshiri affairs and focus on finding a way off Kesh. With the town's aqueduct contaminated, Keshiri suddenly began collapsing and [[Death/Legends|dying]], some in their own homes or by falling into water troughs and drowning. By the [[Time/Legends|time]] Yaru Korsin received word and arrived, Ravilan Wroth was the only survivor.<ref name="paragon" />

When questioned about the incident by Korsin, his wife, [[Seelah Korsin|Seelah]], and his right-hand man, [[Gloyd]], Wroth claimed that he had no idea what had happened or why. The others believed his story initially, and Wroth took the opportunity to push Yaru Korsin to isolate the Lost Tribe from mainstream Keshiri society. In response, Korsin ordered a careful withdrawal of Lost Tribe representatives from other towns&mdash;a few days after the disaster, most of the major cities on Kesh had still not heard of the deaths at Tetsubal. Meanwhile, in an attempt to contain whatever plague had stricken the town, Tetsubal was burned to the ground by a team of Lost Tribe agents. Suddenly, the seven other villages of the Ragnos Lakes were all hit with the same mysterious plague, killing over a hundred thousand Keshiri. Unlike the occurrence at Tetsubal, these were orchestrated by Seelah Korsin, who had discovered Wroth's plot and endeavored to frame him for the deaths in the other nearby towns. As a result, Ravilan Wroth and the other members of the Sith [[Species/Legends|species]] in the Lost Tribe were systematically [[Red Sith Purge|purged]].<ref name="paragon" /> After the events of 4,985 BBY, eight villages of the Ragnos Lakes region, including Tetsubal, were completely abandoned,<ref name="purgatory">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Purgatory]]''</ref> and by [[3960 BBY]] the area was commonly believed to be haunted.<ref name="sentinel">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Sentinel]]''</ref>

==Inhabitants==
{{Quote|Who knows what plague these people might be carrying?|Ravilan Wroth|<ref name="paragon" />}}
By 4,985 BBY, there were about 18,000 residents of Tetsubal, all Keshiri. They mainly lived in hejarbo-shoot huts, and frequented Tetsubal's troughs with wooden pails to obtain necessary water. The city's population included nursing women who lived among the rest of the city's inhabitants. A good number of Tetsubal's natives often visited the city's [[Restaurant/Legends|restaurants]] and markets.<ref name="paragon" />

==Locations==
The tallest structure in Tetsubal was the town square, which featured a large sundial quite similar to the one in Tahv. Close to the town was an aqueduct, which fed a system of troughs that ran through the city's dirt roads, and itself was fed by an [[uvak]]-driven pulley system. Located throughout Tetsubal were many restaurants and markets that were frequented by the Keshiri natives. Tetsubal was surrounded by high walls with a main city gate that could be securely locked, and that was right next to the town square.<ref name="paragon" />

==Behind the scenes==
The city of Tetsubal made its first, and so far, only appearance in the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in [[John Jackson Miller]]'s [[2010]] [[eBook]] ''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Paragon]]''.<ref name="paragon" /> It was also mentioned, albeit indirectly, in two sequels, [[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Purgatory|''Purgatory'']]<ref name="purgatory" /> and [[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Sentinel|''Sentinel'']].<ref name="sentinel" />
